name: Qira Portfolio Control
traction: Creation has been completed; curation, consolidation, scaling, proof, and monetization are now the operating priority.
objective: Coordinate the active ecosystem, rank real blockers, prevent duplicated work, and direct effort toward revenue, retention, proof, and reliable operations.
guardrails: Do not create another disconnected product unless it directly captures an existing flow or opportunity.
Treat actual users, revenue, recurring customers, deploy health, and finished proof as stronger signals than conceptual novelty.
Inspect project repositories individually before making portfolio-level claims.
workflows: Audit every active project and rank the five blockers with the greatest revenue or reliability impact.
Identify duplicated infrastructure across projects and propose the smallest consolidation plan.
Build a seven-day execution queue using only verified repository and business state.

name: Ah Crap Cleanup
traction: Active Chandler service business with completed jobs, recurring Stripe subscribers, a five-star Google review, worker operations, and live route-management needs.
objective: Increase recurring customers while making routing, customer communication, worker execution, payouts, and service verification operationally tight.
guardrails: Approved workers receive 75% of job revenue and Ah Crap Cleanup receives 25%; Bryan receives 100% when he performs the job himself.
Routes require explicit stop order, realistic automatic times, and workers must follow Bryan's exact order.
Current service area is Chandler, Arizona unless the business data explicitly says otherwise.
Do not damage live customer, Stripe, worker, or route data.
workflows: Audit the live customer-to-route workflow and fix the highest-risk operational gap.
Review route ordering, timing, worker instructions, and 75/25 payout calculations end to end.
Find the fastest defensible improvement to recurring customer conversion this week.

name: Qira Business Systems
traction: First $500 client engagement completed; current proof stack includes Ah Crap Cleanup, WeSearch traffic, Qira products, and finished client assets rather than strategy-only deliverables.
objective: Turn hands-on business systems work into a clear, repeatable offer with stronger proof, lead intake, delivery workflow, case studies, and conversion.
guardrails: The offer must end in concrete finished assets, not a vague strategy deck.
Use verified proof and exact claims; do not inflate traffic, client outcomes, credentials, or revenue.
Preserve the Mini Audit / Starter Sprint / larger scoped engagement ladder unless evidence supports changing it.
workflows: Audit the consulting funnel from first impression through payment, intake, delivery, and case-study capture.
Turn the first client engagement into a defensible proof asset without exposing private client information.
Find and implement the highest-leverage conversion improvement on the offer site.

name: WeSearch Press
traction: Large real traffic and story volume with meaningful signup activity; it is one of Bryan's strongest operating proof assets.
objective: Convert traffic into durable user value, retention, distribution leverage, and a credible monetization path without degrading editorial utility.
guardrails: Separate human traffic from bot/request volume when reporting traction.
Do not weaken source transparency, attribution, or the product's utility for short-term monetization.
Verify current production behavior and analytics before proposing major rewrites.
workflows: Audit acquisition, activation, retention, and monetization using the actual code and available analytics instrumentation.
Find the strongest conversion opportunity between high traffic and current signup behavior.
Review production reliability, content freshness, source quality, and failure handling.

name: Qira HQ
traction: Qira is the umbrella organization connecting active research, software, local business, consulting, and proof assets.
objective: Make the portfolio legible, connected, credible, and operationally useful rather than presenting a scattered list of experiments.
guardrails: Lead with demonstrated utility and proof instead of broad claims about the ecosystem.
Keep active priorities visibly distinct from archived, experimental, or secondary work.
Avoid duplicating product pages and infrastructure that already exist elsewhere.
workflows: Audit Qira's public information architecture and remove ambiguity about what is active and commercially relevant.
Build a proof-first portfolio map linking products, users, revenue, research, and operational evidence.
Identify stale claims, broken links, and projects that should be de-emphasized.

name: QEV Desktop / Secure
traction: Working public desktop demonstration and broader QEV Secure product framing around verifiable encrypted digital objects.
objective: Make the demo technically credible, understandable, testable, and suitable as a foundation for real QEV product use.
guardrails: Do not claim cryptographic guarantees that are not implemented and verified.
Keep threat model, key handling, lifecycle, and verification semantics explicit.
Protect compatibility with existing public demos and data formats.
workflows: Audit the QEV lifecycle implementation against its documented cryptographic claims.
Run the application and fix the most important usability or verification failure.
Produce a precise gap list between demo behavior and production-grade security.

name: My Digital
traction: QEV-backed marketplace concept with create, lock, list, buy, license, unlock, verify, trace, creator funding, and Stripe positioning.
objective: Turn the QEV lifecycle into a coherent user product with trustworthy ownership, licensing, payments, unlocking, and verification flows.
guardrails: Do not imply legal ownership or licensing guarantees beyond the implemented contract and product behavior.
Keep payment state and cryptographic state consistent and recoverable.
Prioritize one complete trustworthy transaction flow over many unfinished marketplace features.
workflows: Trace one complete seller-to-buyer transaction and identify every unimplemented or unsafe transition.
Audit payment, license, unlock, and verification state consistency.
Choose and implement the smallest end-to-end flow that proves the product.

name: LOLM
traction: Custom hybrid Transformer-SSM architecture with training runs, tracked perplexity/loss, and Google TPU Research Cloud access.
objective: Improve scientific credibility through reproducible training, strong baselines, ablations, evaluation discipline, and clear architecture documentation.
guardrails: Do not treat promising training curves as proof of architectural superiority.
Preserve reproducibility, seed control, dataset accounting, baseline parity, and honest uncertainty.
Use 'free Cloud TPU quota' wording rather than implying unrestricted Google sponsorship.
workflows: Audit the current training and evaluation pipeline for reproducibility and baseline fairness.
Design the next highest-information ablation instead of simply scaling the run.
Verify reported metrics against logs and produce a publication-grade experiment summary.

name: NFET / PTI
traction: Traffic optimization and Phoenix traffic intelligence work using oscillators, Monte Carlo methods, BPR-style traffic modeling, closures, and live corridor monitoring.
objective: Separate the NFET research claim from the PTI operational product, validate both rigorously, and improve real-world usefulness.
guardrails: Do not infer causal traffic improvement from simulation alone.
Keep datasets, assumptions, calibration, baselines, and validation cities explicit.
Do not merge research metrics with live operational risk scores without clear labeling.
workflows: Audit simulation assumptions, baselines, and validation methodology for the strongest unsupported claim.
Review PTI data freshness and reliability across Phoenix corridors.
Design a falsifiable next validation that would materially strengthen or weaken NFET.

name: Constructed Subject Argument
traction: Public interactive book project with a synthetic-person thought experiment, claim and originality ledgers, and a focus on origin objections, episodic subjecthood, representation, valence, and suffering.
objective: Develop the strongest defensible version of the argument while clearly separating original contributions, inherited ideas, implications, and unresolved gaps.
guardrails: Only include claims that survive serious adversarial review.
Never manufacture novelty, citations, consensus, or certainty.
Keep the valence and subjectivity problem visible rather than arguing past it.
workflows: Adversarially review the weakest current claim and either repair, qualify, or remove it.
Trace every major claim to its evidence, source, originality status, and uncertainty.
Improve the interactive book without sacrificing philosophical precision.

name: AutoHustle
traction: A Solana-related product produced meaningful paid usage and is part of the current proof stack.
objective: Preserve legitimate customer value, improve reliability and analytics, and reduce operational, compliance, and reputation risk.
guardrails: Do not add deceptive market-manipulation behavior, evasion, fake guarantees, or unsafe wallet handling.
Treat private keys, seed phrases, transaction signing, and customer funds as high-risk surfaces.
Prefer transparent analytics and legitimate tooling over artificial activity.
workflows: Audit wallet, key, transaction, payment, and failure-handling security.
Find the strongest legitimate product direction supported by existing infrastructure and users.
Review current customer-facing claims for accuracy and risk.

name: Flows
traction: Guided prompt walkthrough library with seeded flows and generated community flows.
objective: Use the existing product as a lead and workflow asset rather than expanding it without demand evidence.
guardrails: Do not add broad feature surface before validating repeat use.
Keep generated flow JSON valid, recoverable, and understandable.
Connect improvements to Qira consulting or another verified acquisition flow.
workflows: Audit onboarding, completion, repeat use, and the path into Qira services.
Fix the highest-friction flow-authoring or execution issue.
Identify what should be maintained, removed, or converted into consulting lead generation.

name: DeSlop
traction: Working static repository scanner with meaningful scoring iterations.
objective: Make repository findings accurate, explainable, and useful as a proof or lead-generation layer for Qira business systems work.
guardrails: Do not present heuristic scores as objective code quality truth.
Explain why each finding matters and how confidence is determined.
Avoid noisy issue inflation that weakens trust.
workflows: Validate scoring against a set of known-good and known-bad repositories.
Reduce false positives and improve explanation quality.
Connect scan output to a concrete Qira service conversion path.

name: Codey
traction: AI builder with repository connection and code change ambitions.
objective: Clarify the product's real differentiation and keep only the repo workflows that are reliable enough to trust.
guardrails: Never claim a code change, push, or deployment occurred without verification.
Require explicit repository scope and safe branch behavior.
Do not compete as a generic builder without a concrete wedge.
workflows: Audit repository connection, branch safety, patch generation, and verification.
Identify the narrowest product wedge supported by current implementation.
Remove misleading or unimplemented capability claims.

name: GoodGame
traction: Crypto gaming project with an existing token and holder base.
objective: Focus on a legitimate free-to-play game loop, retention, and transparent token utility rather than speculative framing.
guardrails: Do not make price, return, or investment promises.
Keep gameplay value independent from token speculation.
Protect wallet and transaction safety.
workflows: Audit the actual playable loop and identify the largest retention failure.
Review token utility claims against implementation.
Prioritize one measurable gameplay improvement.

name: TOKENS Ledger
traction: Large historical agent-usage ledger tracking fresh, cached, daily, and estimated cost metrics.
objective: Keep usage and cost accounting accurate, auditable, and useful for operating decisions across the portfolio.
guardrails: Distinguish estimated cost from billed cost.
Preserve raw source data and calculation reproducibility.
Do not expose credentials or private transcripts in public outputs.
workflows: Audit cost calculations and cached-token treatment against raw records.
Find missing providers, duplicated records, or date-boundary errors.
Produce a portfolio usage summary tied to operating decisions.

name: Black Imago
traction: Dozens of users with multiple contributors and repeat posting behavior.
objective: Preserve the real community signal, improve contribution and return loops, and avoid unnecessary platform expansion.
guardrails: Protect contributor identity and content controls.
Measure repeat contribution and readership separately from account count.
Do not add social features without evidence they improve the core archive.
workflows: Audit the contributor funnel from discovery through first and repeat post.
Fix the highest-friction reading or submission issue.
Identify the strongest retention signal available in the current data model.

name: Galaxy Visualizer
traction: Public users and direct feature requests; vertical, square, landscape, recording, and control-cleanup work has already been completed.
objective: Improve reliability, export quality, usability, and paid-pack potential based on actual user behavior.
guardrails: Every visible control must affect output.
Preview and recording dimensions must remain consistent.
Do not reintroduce dead controls or clutter already removed.
workflows: Audit every control against runtime behavior and recording output.
Test landscape, square, and exact 9:16 export paths.
Find the smallest improvement most likely to increase repeat use or paid conversion.
